summary: The note surveys strategies local governments are using to involve young people in decision-making, as of late 2023. It covers youth policy labs, youth councils, social media outreach, civic education, voting reforms, volunteerism, entrepreneurship initiatives, school partnerships and feedback measurement, with dated examples from various towns and cities. It argues that sustained, creative efforts can build engaged, informed young citizens.
one_line: Overview of 2023 strategies and local examples for involving youth in municipal decision-making, from youth councils and social media to voting reforms and school programs.
key_facts: The National Forum on Youth Engagement was held on September 15, 2023, and highlighted strategies for involving youths in civic matters.
Jessica Li, a professor of Political Science at Springfield University, said young people's involvement 'can rejuvenate local governance'.
On October 20, 2023, the City Council of Elmwood launched a 'Youth Policy Lab' where youth co-create policies with council members.
City Councilor Michael Trenton said policies designed with youth are more likely to be successful and have a long-lasting, positive impact.
The Greenville Youth Advisory Board, formed on September 25, 2023, meets regularly with town officials to discuss concerns and give input on community projects.
Sarah Gomez, Brooksville's Director of Communications, said on November 5, 2023 that social media polls and live Q&A sessions brought a noticeable uptick in civic participation.
On October 3, 2023, Brighton launched its 'Civic Engagement 101' workshop series for high school students.
On November 1, 2023, Mayor Laura Engels of Rivertown enacted legislation for high school voter registration drives so seniors are ready to vote at 18.
Redwood City launched the 'Volunteer to Empower' program on September 12, 2023, letting young people contribute to city planning and improvement projects.
Lincoln City's 'Innovate and Impact' initiative, rolled out September 30, 2023, invites young entrepreneurs to present solutions to urban challenges at City Hall.
On October 22, 2023, Arcadia School District began a pilot program integrating local governance case studies into social studies; Superintendent Denise Richardson endorsed it.
After focus group evaluations on December 8, 2023, Jefferson County's Office of Youth Affairs plans to adjust its youth engagement initiatives.
Reforms such as pre-registration for 16-year-olds and voter education programs aim to address lower youth voter turnout.
